stages.name: Stage 1, diagnosis
notes: Paired bootstrap, model minus baseline, lower is better.
Poisson raw against Elo only is Brier +0.0663 [+0.0585, +0.0735], so the Poisson champion is worse.
Poisson raw against base rate is -0.0539 [-0.0605, -0.0476], so it beats the base rate.
Poisson + temperature against Poisson raw is Brier +0.0000 [-0.0007, +0.0007], so calibration changes nothing measurable.
The accuracy of the uniform and base-rate rows is the home-win share, because both always pick home.

stages.name: Stage 2, held-out test
notes: Elo ordinal against Poisson raw, paired bootstrap, 2023 to 2025, is Brier -0.0728 [-0.0836, -0.0623], RPS -0.0320 [-0.0364, -0.0278] and log loss -0.1113 [-0.1271, -0.0955].
The Brier interval is below 0 in each of the three years.
On the held-out years the mean predicted draw rate is 0.224 for Elo ordinal and 0.283 for Poisson raw, against 0.233 observed.
The gain comes from using Elo, not from the fitted draw model.
Elo ordinal against plain Elo only is Brier -0.0015 [-0.0025, -0.0004] on the held-out years, and over 2018 to 2025 (selection years included) it is -0.0003 [-0.0010, +0.0003].
The report treats the two Elo rules as equivalent in accuracy and prefers the fitted one for serving because its draw rate is calibrated and it comes with a coherent score matrix.
A blend with the Poisson 1X2 added nothing.
